title: Adversarial review of W0-CONTRACTS (contracts)
final_text:
The work is complete. Here is the summary.

## What I did

I reviewed `src/minireason/loop/contracts.py` (W0-CONTRACTS) adversarially against `notes/WAVE0-INTERFACE.md`, `design/design-s2-roles-and-guard.md` (§2.3, §2.4 G1/G4/G9/D4/G12) and `design/design-s7-wave-plan.md`'s W0-CONTRACTS acceptance clause, cross-checking against `standard.py`, `types.py`, `use_relation_h005.py` and `deepreason_core.harness`. Every finding was executed as a probe, not asserted.

## Files written (all under the sandbox root; nothing under `src/` was touched)

- `review/contracts.md` — the review.
- `probe/` — thirteen probe scripts: `p01_totality`, `p02_exceptions`, `p03_outside_vocabulary`, `p04_g12`, `p04b_warrant`, `p05_identity`, `p06_schemas`, `p06b_restore`, `p07_transcript`, `p08_shapes`, `p09_headers`, `p10_misc`, `p11_roundtrip`, `p12_aggregate`, plus an empty `probe/__init__.py`.

## Findings (ordered BLOCKER → SHOULD-FIX → NOTE, unranked within a class)

- **BLOCKER: none reproduced.** Three candidate seams attacked and held (see below).

- **F1 (SHOULD-FIX)** — The published "same objects" (`contracts.SCHEMAS`/the five role schemas/`WORD_LIMITS` are `standard`'s own) are mutable *in place* through a `MappingProxyType` that guards only the top level. A one-line `contracts.DEFENDER_SCHEMA["required"].clear()` turns `check("defender", {})` into a `KeyError` escaping the function whose docstring says **"Never raises"**, and does not move the pinned `STANDARD_BODY_SHA256`/`ROLE_SCHEMAS_SHA256`. Probe `p06b_restore.py` shows the mutation breaking the seam and the digest staying pinned to the pre-mutation schemas. Repair: structurally freeze the schemas before the validators are built.

- **F2 (NOTE)** — `VARIATOR_SCHEMA` is `minItems:1, uniqueItems` with no `maxItems`; a 3-paraphrase output validates even though `TRIAL_PARAPHRASE_N = 2` is a pinned guard parameter. **F3 (NOTE)** — `AGGREGATE_KEYS` is schema-side only and probed so; numeric artifact *content* passes both guards by design, but the module docstring's "no aggregate" sentence could mislead. **F4 (NOTE)** — `SCHEMA_REASONS` is complete: every reason `check()` emits is in the table, all 18 reachable and spelled in the right grain. **F5 (NOTE)** — the O2 `verdict`/`FORBIDDEN_KEYS` collision is real in this sandbox (`p04b_warrant.py`: the guard refuses the vendored `Warrant` record at path `('verdict',)`), and the pinning test named in the notes is not shipped in this snapshot.

- **Tried, and could not break** (three, executed): (1) `check()`'s never-raises totality across boundary inputs including non-JSON text, bad UTF-8, and `MappingProxyType` bodies; (2) G4/D6 normalisation passes the vendored `conforming_transcript` gate exactly at the designed boundaries and round-trips; (3) the G12 guard across all three subjects (case-folded nested keys, bare `str` refusal, and `assert_no_scoring_headers` on contiguous/implicit tables and headings).

The review also records what was verified to hold: one-owner identity by `is`, the digest pin, the exception conventions, purity/determinism, and `SCHEMA_REASONS` completeness.

## Result of the last test run

All thirteen probes ran clean, each printing the executed evidence quoted verbatim in the review. `python3 run_tests.py` → `Ran 0 tests in 0.000s / OK` — no test modules are shipped in this frozen snapshot (a direct `python3 run_tests.py tests.loop.test_contracts` fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tests.loop.test_contracts'`, which the review notes against the test-file claims in the interface).
